title: The Morphogenetic Field and the Ki-Net: A Structural Convergence Between Sheldrake's Field Theory and Katayama's Dual-Layer Cosmology
abstract: Rupert Sheldrake proposed in 1981 that biological form is not fully determined by genetic code alone, but is shaped by "morphogenetic fields" — spatial structures that pre-exist and guide the development of living organisms. Independently, Katayama Yoshimitsu developed the "Ki-Net" (気の網) hypothesis: that material design is pre-embedded in cosmic space as an information network, and that particles, life, and phenomena emerge in accordance with this pre-existing structure. This paper demonstrates that these two theories, developed independently across different disciplines and decades, share an identical structural framework. title: The Master-Embedded Device: Transmitting Tacit Knowledge Density Through AI Agent Architecture
abstract: This paper proposes a framework for embedding the tacit knowledge density of a master craftsperson, philosopher, or domain expert into an AI agent architecture — creating a "Master-Embedded Device." The core hypothesis is that expertise is not primarily explicit knowledge (rules, manuals, procedures), but tacit density: the accumulated pattern of judgment, proportion, timing, and aesthetic discrimination that cannot be verbalized but can be observed and modeled. An AI agent trained on sufficient observations of a master's decisions can function as a carrier of that density, making it accessible to non-masters and preserving it beyond the master's lifespan. This framework is situated within the V=N/D value density theory and the broader SYSTEM YOSHIMITSU KATAYAMA civilizational architecture

title: The Master-Embedded Device v3.0: Toward a Peer-Reviewable Framework for Tacit Knowledge Transfer into AI Agent Systems
abstract: This paper proposes the "Master-Embedded Device" — an AI agent architecture in which the tacit knowledge of a domain expert is structurally transferred to enable successors to begin at a higher baseline of output quality with lower learning friction. We extend Polanyi's (1966) proximal-distal knowledge taxonomy with Collins's (2010) critique that tacit knowledge is fundamentally social rather than individual, and argue that while full transfer is impossible, **partial transfer of distal and approximated proximal knowledge** produces measurably different agent baselines than distal-only transfer. title: Location-Based Cryptographic Authentication: A Coordinate-as-Key Protocol for Physical Presence Verification
abstract: This paper proposes a novel cryptographic authentication protocol in which physical geographic coordinates serve as the cryptographic key. Unlike conventional password-based systems where authentication requires only knowledge (a secret string), the Coordinate-as-Key (CaK) protocol requires physical presence at a specific GPS location. The key cannot be replicated remotely — it is bound to existence in space, not to knowledge alone. This creates an entirely new category of authentication: Presence-Bound Cryptography (PBC).
keywords: theoretical physics, cosmology, genki particle, Ki field, KOKU universe, dual-layer light, TheYKHC, Yoshimitsu Katayama, ORCID:0009-0006-2290-6593

title: The Line of Succession Hypothesis: Civilization as Intergenerational Density Transfer
abstract: This paper proposes the Line of Succession Hypothesis: that civilization is not primarily an accumulation of material wealth, technological capability, or institutional structure, but an ongoing process of intergenerational density transfer — the transmission of N (meaningful action density) from those who have accumulated it to those who have not yet done so. The hypothesis draws on the author's V=N/D value density theory, the moral framework of Hiroi Chikuro (広池千九郎), the author's personal inheritance from his father Masatada Katayama, and the observed structure of the SYSTEM YOSHIMITSU KATAYAMA civilizational architecture. The core claim is that civilization advances when density transfer succeeds and declines when it fails.
keywords: theoretical physics, cosmology, genki particle, Ki field, KOKU universe, dual-layer light, TheYKHC, Yoshimitsu Katayama, ORCID:0009-0006-2290-6593
